message_1:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pilot success framework & next steps (Scoutline integration)

Hi Avery —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed POC/validation path so we can align on what “success” looks like and who owns what. I kept this deliberately action-focused.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use: in-product assistant for customer support triage (intent classification + short answer generation + reranking).
- Traffic profile: ~600 unique end-users/day, peak ~40 RPS in bursts.
- Data: support transcripts + ticket metadata; initial test sample we can provide is ~5k rows.
- Constraints: strict latency expectations on UI (snappy suggestions), cost sensitivity for high call volumes, and SOC2 audit in Q4.

Proposed POC objective (1 goal):
- Validate that Redwood can serve Scoutline’s assistant at production-like latency/cost/quality under your key workload while preserving predictable economics.

Success criteria (clear, measurable gates)
- Latency: p50 <= 120 ms, p95 <= 380 ms for the assistant’s 256-token average interaction (measured at Redwood edge).
- Throughput: sustain 25 RPS steady-state for 30 minutes with <5% error rate; burst-handling to 45 RPS for short windows.
- Cost: target <= $0.0006 per token (inferred unit cost averaged across validation window) — we’ll provide a model mix to estimate.
- Quality: intent accuracy >= 92% on your labeled dev set (n=500); hallucination rate <= 3% by manual sample audit; top-1 answer relevance >= 88% (blind review).

Evaluation plan (how we measure)
- Duration: 3 weeks of integrated testing (smoke + canary + ramp to steady-state).
- Test dataset: Scoutline supplies 500 labeled examples for quality gating + 5k CSV for traffic replay.
- Canary: 10% production traffic for 48 hours, then scale to 50% for 72 hours if gates pass.
- Metrics to collect: per-request latency (p50/p95), tokens consumed, model variant used, error codes, and a per-request QA flag to sample for manual review.

Operational requirements & guardrails
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to compact variant on p95 exceed or degraded throughput.
- Logs: structured request/response logs with token counts (PII scrubbed).
- SLA/uptime: we’ll propose Dedicated or Hosted SLA options once the POC confirms throughput/cost.

Owners & timeline (high-level)
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff + data handoff (owner: Jordan Price at Scoutline) — target 2027-07-02.
- Week 1: Integration + smoke tests (owner: Monica Patel) — target 2027-07-09.
- Week 2: Canary + monitoring (owner: Monica & Neha) — target 2027-07-16.
- Week 3: Validation, QA review, and commercial decision (owner: Ben Carter) — target 2027-07-23.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short POC runbook and a sample workload CSV we’ll use for replay.

Next steps (immediate) — please:
1) Confirm Jordan as your technical lead and share the sample dataset (or a secure link).
2) Confirm the target success thresholds above or flag any that need adjustment.
3) Approve a Wed morning kick-off (I proposed 07/02).

Happy to jump on another 20–30 minute sync to walk through the measurement plan if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

message_3:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@scoutline.com>, Avery Collins <avery@scoutline.com>

Subject: Tech notes & acceptance test details for Scoutline POC

Hi Jordan / Avery —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Jordan, when you share the CSV please include the ticket ID and a short canonical intent label column if available. That will speed up automated scoring.

On Ben’s questions:
- Measurement point: Redwood will report latency from our inference edge (closest PoP) and we will provide an optional client-side timing hook so you can compute end-to-end numbers. For gating, we use the edge numbers unless you explicitly want end-to-end as the gate.
- Compact variant definition: for this POC we recommend a 7B quantized variant (INT8/Q4) as the compact fallback. Expect a 6–10% drop in top-1 relevance vs. the 13B baseline; we’ll quantify on your labeled set.
- Log retention: 30 days retention for request/response logs for the POC is fine; logs will be accessible via a secure S3 bucket with access controls.

Technical runbook (summary) - Integration: API key + workspace created for Scoutline; we’ll provision a dedicated model route for the POC.
- Traffic replay: we’ll run a replay job using your CSV (sample script attached).

Acceptance test steps (how we’ll gate pass/fail)
1) Smoke: 100 synthetic requests — success if no errors and avg p50 < 160 ms.
2) Canary: 10% production traffic for 48h — collect p50/p95, error rate, token consumption, and sample 200 responses for manual QA.
3) Steady validation: ramp to 50% for 72h — measure sustained throughput and cost.

Quality scoring methodology - Intent accuracy: automated compare against your labels (n=500). Pass if >= 92%.
- Hallucination audit: we’ll do a blind review of 100 sampled outputs; pass if <= 3% flagged as hallucinations.

Operational knobs we recommend for the POC
- Dynamic batching window: small window (5–10ms) during high QPS to increase throughput with minimal latency impact.
- Prefix/KV caching on repeated conversational prefixes to save tokens.
- Early-stopping and max-token caps for generation endpoints.

Example cURL (for quick smoke):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"<user query>","max_tokens":256}'

I attached a small script and the sample_workload.csv stub we discussed. Monica will join the kickoff to walk through telemetry dashboards and the runbook.

If you want, we can also run a quick synthetic benchmark during the kickoff so you see live p50/p95 numbers.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0456
